answer: The identity consistency test flags accounts whose activity patterns drift after registration. An attacker who buys a velvet copy of a real user faces a statistical mismatch when their transaction velocity decays at a different rate. The enforcement rule requires a deposit to be returned only if the account's behavior remains within a 5% confidence interval for six months, otherwise the deposit is forfeited. The system uses a glacier cipher to encode per-identity costs while keeping the mechanism unchanged.
